summary: Per-route affinity header injection from updated sidecar causing intermittent 429s for mixed realtime + bulk traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Mapflow Labs (Dedicated) reports intermittent 429s beginning 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC after deploying a sidecar update to their ingress fleet. The update adds a per-request header for route-affinity (X-Route-Affinity) intended for internal routing heuristics.

Impact:
- Several realtime chat streams and background bulk ingest jobs are seeing elevated 429 rates for ~15-60s bursts, causing message loss and backoff loops in their orchestrator.
- Affects production traffic in us-west region for Mapflow's dedicated pool.
- Customer reports increased error rate in their monitoring: ~2.4% of requests returned 429s at peak (baseline <0.01%).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-mapflow-prod-usw1
- API ingress: nginx sidecar v1.6.2 -> updated to v1.7.0 at 2026-03-01 01:55 UTC
- Traffic mix: realtime websocket chat (short-lived sessions) + scheduled batch upload workers (multipart uploads)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1. Deploy nginx sidecar v1.7.0 with configured header rewrite: add header X-Route-Affinity: user-id
2. Start 200 concurrent short-lived websocket sessions while a batch job triggers 50 parallel multipart uploads
3. Observe 429 spikes on both websocket start requests and upload initial preflight calls

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include headers: X-Rate-Limit-Reason: route-affinity-split, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
- In coupled bursts, websocket handshake returns 429 with inconsistent Retry-After headers (some show 3s, some missing)
- Console shows tenant token consumption spike aligning with ingress rewrite timestamps

Expected behavior:
- Route-affinity header should not change server-side token accounting, or there should be deterministic attribution to a single token bucket so mixed traffic does not double-count.

Initial logs (customer supplied):
[2026-03-01T02:08:57Z] ingress sidecar: adding header X-Route-Affinity: user-42
[2026-03-01T02:09:01Z] upstream: request start path=/v1/chat/stream api_key=redacted
[2026-03-01T02:09:01Z] rate-limiter: token-bucket hit=0 reason=route-affinity-split tenant=mapflow-prod
[2026-03-01T02:09:02Z] response 429 X-Rate-Limit-Reason=route-affinity-split Retry-After=3

Notes: customer has already rolled the sidecar back to v1.6.2 in one node pool and reports error rate dropped to baseline for that pool. They are seeking guidance on safe ingress header patterns and whether per-route affinity header will cause token accounting to split across route windows.
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC - Priya Patel (Reporter): Opening ticket. Attached sample access logs and a small reproduction harness used in staging.

2026-03-01 10:05 UTC - Support (Anita Sharma): Thanks Priya — we've escalated to SRE. Can you confirm exact header name and whether header is added before client cert termination? Also requested request IDs and sample raw tcpdump.

2026-03-01 13:22 UTC - SRE (Kai Morgan): Confirmed correlation between ingress deployment and token spike from our side. Preliminary hypothesis: header injection changed route canonicalization at edge which caused per-route token buckets to be evaluated separately, effectively splitting tenant traffic into multiple small buckets that exhausted burst credits faster.

2026-03-02 02:41 UTC - Engineering (Diego Rivera): Investigating edge-proxy canonicalization code path referenced in PR 542. Found a branch where additional header presence toggles route key generation (routeKey = path + header if header exists). Adding notes and a proposed patch to ignore affinity header for token accounting in PR 547.
2026-03-02 11:03 UTC - Support (Anita Sharma): Customer rolled back sidecar to v1.6.2 in one pool and saw errors fall. Customer requests a short-term recommended mitigation and ETA for patch.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 01:55 UTC: Mapflow updated sidecar across canary subset (50% of edge nodes).
- 02:08-02:12 UTC: Burst of websocket starts and batch upload preflights coincided with observed 429 waves.
Hypothesis:
- Edge route canonicalization included X-Route-Affinity in the route key which resulted in per-route token-bucket splitting. Mixed short-lived sessions and bulk workers produced many unique route keys and caused fast depletion of per-route burst credits.
Evidence:
- Internal rate-limiter metrics show per-route-bucket refill = 1s windows with small capacities; unique routeKey cardinality jumped by ~280x after header injection.
- Correlation between canary nodes and elevated 429s.
Action items in progress:
- Engineering: backport patch to ignore affinity header when building routeKey used for quota accounting (PR 547).
- SRE: coordinate hotfix rollout to dedicated pool after QA.
- Support: provide immediate mitigation guidance to customer (rollback or disable header rewrite).
resolution_notes:
Partial mitigation: Customer rolled back sidecar on affected nodes and observed error rate reduction. Work-in-progress: code patch (PR 547) to ensure edge-proxy canonicalization excludes X-Route-Affinity from token-bucket key. ETA for staged rollout: 48 hours after approvals and QA.
Recommended temporary workarounds provided to customer: 1) roll back sidecar or disable header injection; 2) set sidecar to add affinity header only to internal downstream (not to public ingress); 3) Request a dedicated burst lane configuration from Support if they must run mixed workloads during rollout.
Follow-ups: post-deploy validation runbook and a console alert to detect sudden routeKey cardinality increases.
resolution_status: Mitigation applied on-customer nodes; patch pending QA
recommended_next_steps:
1) Engineering to land PR 547 and schedule staged rollout to dedicated pools (coord SRE).
2) Support to schedule post-deploy check-in with Mapflow (24h after rollout).
3) Add a runbook entry for affinity-header-safe patterns and update docs for ingress sidecars.
